pipeline: if language != en: translate text -> English via NLLB-200
classify English text with the emotion model -> one of 6 DAIR labels

multilingual_eval.note: Stratified 60-row DAIR test slice (10 per emotion). The SAME rows were machine-translated into natural text in each of the 20 languages (forward via gpt-oss-20b), then translated back to English by the runtime translator (NLLB-200-distilled-1.3B) and classified. Gold = original English DAIR label. Per-language n=60 is directional (noisy); the ship decision rests on the pooled macro-F1 across all 20 (n=1200).

translator_comparison_pooled_macro_f1.note: Same DistilBERT classifier + same gold across all rows; methods differ only in the translator (or, for llm_direct, replace the whole pipeline). NLLB-1.3B selected as the best.

multilingual_eval.selection_rationale: NLLB-1.3B wins pooled (+1.7pp over 600M, better in 13/20 langs) and is free, local, 0 API calls. LLM-as-translator (20B 0.80, 120B 0.88) both scored BELOW NLLB pooled AND cost an API call per message against the shared 15 req/min budget. LLM-direct (~0.49) is confounded (DistilBERT is fine-tuned on DAIR, so a zero-shot LLM is graded out-of-distribution). Knowledge distillation considered but not pursued: it reopens the no-fine-tuning constraint and its supervision is still NLLB-bottlenecked (uncertain accuracy gain).
